title: The dev front answers unknown module paths with HTML, so a page module's failure is silent
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui, 2026-09-23, driving the merged router on the front the owner actually uses (:5173).

THE DEFECT: the page's modules are served by the SERVER from SOURCE_DIRS = [core, browser, tools, tests, lib] (server.mjs:765) and the browser imports them as ABSOLUTE paths (/core/paths.ts, /lib/channel.mjs, /browser/worker.ts). The dev front proxied only /browser, so every other one of those requests fell through to Vite, and Vite answered with its SPA fallback: MEASURED, /core/paths.ts via :5173 -> 200 text/html, 16 KB, with /@vite/client in the body; via :8787 -> 200 text/javascript, 3.6 KB. A module worker cannot execute an HTML document, so the environment page's worker never loaded its module graph, never answered the host hello, and window.e1m0.ready stayed pending forever: THE PAGE LOOKED ALIVE AND COULD NOT ACT AT ALL.

WHY IT SURVIVED: every page test drives the page against the SERVER'S OWN PORT (startServer's base), which never touches Vite. So the suite is green and the front is broken — the instrument-measuring-the-adjacent-class shape again, same as the #send button (a text state, not a capability state) and the sparse audio feed (clearing, not stepping).

FIXED IN THIS LANE, minimising: the five SOURCE_DIRS prefixes are now proxied in vite.config.js (commit f852e7e, cherry-picked onto the landing line; content-identical to 1b1816d on feat/page-writes-room). /channel was added in the same commit — the executor channel was ALSO unproxied, which made a page-owned root report executor.connected:false and told the user 'The tab that holds this folder is not open' WHILE THE TAB WAS OPEN.

WHAT IS STILL OWED (not done, and bigger than the two-line fix): a general answer to 'the front must serve whatever the server serves for the page, or fail loudly'. A prefix list can drift again — it did once already — and the failure is silent HTML rather than an error. The options are a shared list read by both sides, or a front-side check that a module request returns JavaScript (and says so when it does not).

PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED BY THE ROUTER: no page-owned-root feature could ever have worked through :5173. The router exposed it by making the page's worker load-bearing.
close_reason:
LANDED: the specific breakage in f852e7e (/channel and the module prefixes proxied) and the GENERAL fix in cfe88e1 — both in main, verified by reading main's files (lib/browser-sources.mjs carries the one list; tools/page-acceptance.mjs carries the module-graph check).

THE DEFECT: the page's modules are served by the SERVER from SOURCE_DIRS = [core, browser, tools, tests, lib] and the browser imports them as absolute paths (/core/paths.ts, /lib/channel.mjs, /browser/worker.ts). The dev front proxied only /browser, so every other request fell through to Vite, which answered with its SPA fallback: MEASURED, /core/paths.ts via :5173 -> 200 text/html, 16 KB, with /@vite/client in it; via :8787 -> 200 text/javascript, 3.6 KB. A module worker cannot execute an HTML document, so it died silently — window.e1m0.ready never resolved and THE PAGE LOOKED ALIVE AND COULD NOT ACT AT ALL. Pre-existing: no page-owned-root feature could ever have worked on :5173; the router exposed it by making the page's worker load-bearing.

THE GENERAL FIX, which is what made this closable rather than patched: lib/browser-sources.mjs holds the list ONCE — server.mjs imports it (it serves those directories) and vite.config.js imports it (it must forward them), so the two cannot drift — and tools/page-acceptance.mjs fetches one real module per prefix THROUGH THE FRONT and requires JavaScript, so the next drift fails by name instead of silently.

FALSIFIED AGAINST THE REAL DEFECT rather than a synthetic mutation: a scratch front built from the pre-fix commit bc200f3 (no /core proxy), and the acceptance tool pointed at it, failed naming /core/agent-settings.ts, /tools/acp-check.mjs, /tests/acp-browser.test.mjs and /lib/acp-client.mjs each '200 text/html (the SPA fallback)' — while /browser, which WAS proxied pre-fix, passed. A blanket failure would have proved less; the partial one matching the defect exactly is what shows the check discriminates.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PROTECT AGAINST, stated where the fix lives: a module the page imports from a directory the server does not serve at all. The list only covers what the server knows about — the class is now LOUD rather than silent, which is the honest claim and not 'impossible'.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
COORD'S FRAMING (2026-09-23), which is the right one and is now this bead's headline claim: **the dev front's SPA fallback answers unknown module paths with HTML, so a page module's failure is silent.**

THE CONSEQUENCE, stated as scope rather than as an incident: THE FRONT AND THE TESTED PORT HAVE DIVERGED ENOUGH FOR A WHOLE FEATURE TO BE UNTESTABLE WHERE THE OWNER USES IT. Every page test drives the server's own port; the owner's URL is this front. A page-owned-root feature could never have worked through :5173, and nothing in the suite could notice — the router exposed that by making the page's worker load-bearing, but it did not create it.

THE FAILURE MODE, in the words that make it recognisable: a 200 that means 'here is the app' answering a request for a module — and a failure with NO ERROR, because the thing that failed was the LOADING rather than the code. The page looked alive and could not act at all, which is the worst possible state for anybody debugging it, including its owner.

WHAT LANDED HERE (f852e7e, cherry-picked onto the landing line; content-identical to 1b1816d): /channel proxied (the executor channel — unproxied, a page-owned root reported executor.connected:false and the room told the user 'The tab that holds this folder is not open' WHILE THE TAB WAS OPEN), and the five SOURCE_DIRS prefixes proxied so the page's modules stop being answered with HTML.

STILL OWED, and it is the reason this bead exists rather than being closed by that commit: a prefix list can drift, and it has already drifted once. The two honest options are (a) ONE list read by both the server and the front, or (b) a front-side assertion that a module request answers with JavaScript and says so loudly when it does not. Until one of them exists, the next unproxied path fails the same silent way.

title: The room says WHO acts: the four sentences held for the page-writes router
description:

title: Outer ring: the contour steps once per chunk — fixed and measured four independent ways
description:
LANDED BY voicebox-ui on coord's instruction (the ring lane had finished its branch): fix/outer-ring-janky-smoothing rebased onto main and pushed as c2d180d, gate ALL CLEAR, served tree moved to main.

THE CHANGE (one file, +7/-1): smooth(meter.output, meter.smoothOutput, 0.3) moved out of followPlayback() — which returns early unless a new chunk has started playing — into level(), which the meters() requestAnimationFrame loop calls per rendered frame. So the shift stays discrete per chunk and the contour's blend runs every frame.

CLAIM VERIFIED VS ASSUMED: the commit says 'every frame', so before landing I checked that level() is reached from a requestAnimationFrame loop (public/fused.js meters()). It is.

MEASURED, BOTH DIRECTIONS, FOUR INSTRUMENTS (old = a32ae62, new = c2d180d; identical synthetic audio driven into the page's own playback path, 100 ms chunks back to back so playback never gaps, no vendor and no provider spend):
  1. Ring geometry, rotation removed (64 on-curve points per frame, best circular alignment): old 0.078, 0.037, 0.763 / 0.091, 0.022, 0.574 — frozen then a spike, once per chunk; new 0.481, 0.371, 0.474, 0.469, 0.450 — every frame.
  2. Pixels (consecutive frames blended, mean luma of the difference): old 0.01 0.01 0.06 0.02 0.02 … repeating; new 0.06 0.06 0.07 0.07 … every frame. 6x in the still frames.
  3. cap-ds-flash, per-frame normalised RMSE (independent lane, blind A/B): old spread 5.7x with spikes ~3x typical, ~7 frames apart (≈117 ms ≈ one chunk); new spread 1.2x, no spikes, no identical pairs.
  4. cap-ds-flash, full-circumference 64-ray radius profile with rotation alignment (1024/1024 angle samples covered): old spike train 0.08-1.44 px, 18x spread, spikes 7 pairs apart ≈114 ms, and the spikes SURVIVE rotation alignment (1.44 -> 1.31) so the change is the contour, not rigid rotation; new uniform 1.10-2.08 px, spread 1.9x, no near-zero pair, and alignment removes a little of it (rotation, shared with the old build). Its caveat, kept: the circle-fit residual is ~19 px, so the values are displacement along each sampled ray, not a strict radius.

TWO INSTRUMENTS WERE THROWN AWAY FIRST, and that is part of the record: 'does the drawing move?' cannot discriminate the builds at all (98.7% vs 100% of frames move — the render phase eases per frame in both), and a sparse 4-chunks/s feed is invalid because playback GAPS at that cadence, the page returns to not-speaking, and the ring is CLEARED between chunks — so that run was measuring clearing, not stepping.

VIDEO for the owner's eye: /tmp/vb-ring-vision/handover2/ (A = old, B = new, blind labelling), each 192-193 compositor frames at 60 fps captured via Page.startScreencast, plus a 16-frame strip. The visual read is routed to a vision-capable lane; three of the four instruments above are numeric, and the numbers are the claim.

THE EVIDENCE, five instruments, and one of them a pair of eyes:
  1. ring geometry with rotation removed (mine): old 0.078, 0.037, 0.763 / 0.091, 0.022, 0.574 — frozen then a spike per chunk; new 0.481, 0.371, 0.474, 0.469, 0.450 — every frame.
  2. pixel blend, mean luma of consecutive-frame difference (mine): old 0.01 0.01 0.06 0.02 0.02 … repeating; new 0.06 0.06 0.07 0.07 … every frame — 6x in the still frames.
  3. per-frame normalised RMSE (cap-ds-flash, blind): old spread 5.7x with spikes ~3x typical, ~7 frames apart (~117 ms ~ one chunk); new spread 1.2x, no spikes, no identical pairs.
  4. full-circumference 64-ray radius profile with rotation alignment (cap-ds-flash, blind): old spike train 0.08-1.44 px, 18x spread, spikes 7 pairs apart and SURVIVING rotation alignment (so the change is the contour, not rigid rotation); new uniform 1.10-2.08 px, 1.9x spread, no near-zero pair.
  5. the visual read (gemini lane, blind): A frozen with JUMPS AT FRAMES 03 AND 10; B a travelling crest, zero stagnant frames — the same two moments as the numeric spike pairs (02->03, 09->10).
TWO INSTRUMENTS WERE THROWN AWAY FIRST and are part of the record: 'does the drawing move?' cannot discriminate the builds at all (98.7% vs 100% of frames move — the render phase eases per frame in both), and a sparse 4-chunks/s feed is invalid because playback GAPS at that cadence, the page returns to not-speaking and the ring is CLEARED between chunks — that run was measuring clearing, not stepping.

THREE NARROWINGS CAME AFTER THE AGREEMENT, all by measurement: the lane's own attribution limit (its metric supports 'the ring moves' but not independently 'the contour deforms'); my reflow hypothesis, disproved by its page-level probes; and its solved-centroid measurement, which resolved to 'the ring's centre is a constant in the code (OUTPUT_CENTRE) and the container is pixel-static, so every centre number is a summary statistic of an asymmetric travelling contour'. The discriminator was never the centre — it was the cadence.

THE OWNER-FACING ARTIFACT: /tmp/vb-ring-vision/handover2/ring-before-and-after.mp4 (3.2 s real time, 60 fps screencast frames) plus a quarter-speed cut, built with ffmpeg and no provider spend.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
TWO CORRECTIONS TO HOW THIS EVIDENCE SHOULD BE READ — from cap-ds-flash, the lane that produced instruments 3 and 4, and worth more than the agreement itself. Recorded rather than folded in because the pair of instruments is NOT two independent proofs of one claim.

1. ATTRIBUTION LIMITS OF THE RAY PROFILE. While fitting each frame's circle it also got the ring's CENTRE, and the centres are not equally stable: A's centre moves ~0.3 px in x, B's drifts ~5.7 px in x (379.8 -> 374.1) and ~2.4 px in y. Since the metric is displacement of the hairline ALONG RAYS from that fitted centre, a rigid translation of the whole ring registers exactly like a contour change. So: A's spikes CANNOT be translation (its centre is essentially fixed - that half is clean, and the spikes surviving rotation alignment corroborates it), but B's uniform 1.10-2.08 px could be partly rigid motion. 'The ring moves 1.10-2.08 px every frame' is what the ray profile supports; 'the contour deforms smoothly every frame' is what the SVG instrument supports (64 path points, rotation removed, in the path's own coordinate space). They agree; they do not independently prove the same thing; the ray profile is the weaker of the two for the attribution.

2. WHY THE RING COULD BE TRANSLATING AT ALL, which the numbers alone do not say: the ring is drawn in its own fixed viewBox, so a moving fitted centre most likely means the ring is moving IN THE PAGE (layout reflow as the state text changes width), not deforming. That cannot affect the SVG instrument - it samples the path's own geometry, not its screen position - which is why the two instruments are complementary rather than duplicative.

3. AND THE RECONCILIATION IT ASKED FOR IS ALREADY DONE, WITH FRAME INDICES RATHER THAN ADJECTIVES. It asked that the visual reader name frame pairs rather than describe. The vision-capable lane reported: A frozen frames 00-02, JUMP at frame 03, frozen 04-09, JUMP at frame 10, frozen 11-15. This lane's ray-profile spikes are at pairs 02->03 and 09->10. Same frames.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
POINT 2 CORRECTED: MY REFLOW EXPLANATION IS DISPROVED, BY MEASUREMENT, BY THE LANE THAT PRODUCED THE NUMBERS IT WAS MEANT TO EXPLAIN.

I hypothesised that the ring's fitted centre was drifting because the ring was moving IN THE PAGE (layout reflow as the state text changed width). cap-ds-flash measured it rather than accepting it: ring bbox centre per frame against two page-level structures in the same frames (the wide bottom band y470-541 and the waveform region y270-460).

  A: ring cx 372.5 -> 373.0 (spread 0.50 px)  | band cx 378.00 spread 0.00 | wave cx 378.50 spread 0.00
  B: ring cx 378.0 -> 372.5 (spread 5.50 px)  | band cx 378.00 spread 0.00 | wave cx 378.50 spread 0.00

Both page-level structures are PIXEL-IDENTICAL IN X in all 16 frames of both builds. So page-level layout did not move in this window and a general reflow is not supported. What the numbers do support: the motion is in the ring's OWN drawing. (Its honest limit, kept: two page-level probes are not proof that nothing page-level moved - a movement confined to the ring's own container would look the same.)

AND TWO DETAILS THAT SHARPEN IT, both of which make the fix's mechanism MORE visible, not less:
  - A's 0.5 px centre step lands at FRAME 10 - the same frame as its second contour spike. So A's centre summary moves on the chunk cadence too, like everything else about A.
  - B starts exactly at the page centre (378.0, the same x as the band and the waveform) and drifts to 372.5 by frame 15 - i.e. B ends where A sits. B's drift is concentrated in frames 10-15 while its contour advanced uniformly across ALL pairs, so B has two things happening at once.

MOST LIKELY EXPLANATION, offered as such and NOT as a measurement: every circular summary of this ring (bbox centre, Kasa fit centre) is biased by the contour's shape, because the contour is an asymmetric closed curve with a travelling crest - and the vision-capable lane described exactly that in B: a travelling bulge rotating smoothly round a ring whose circle stays put. If that is right, the centre drift is the crest's travel seen through a summary statistic, not the circle moving. It stays a hypothesis until somebody measures the drawn centre directly (the path is constructed as centre + r(theta)*u(theta) with known angles, so a least-squares solve for the centre per frame is available to anyone who wants it).

RECORD-KEEPING POINT, which is the actual lesson: a hypothesis offered as a hypothesis got measured and failed, and the failure is now in the same place as the evidence it explained. That is the second time today a lane narrowed its own or another's claim at the cost of some tidiness (the first being the attribution limit from the same lane), and both are worth more than the agreement.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CENTRE QUESTION CLOSED — AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THERE WAS NEVER ANY REAL CENTRE MOTION TO EXPLAIN. Do not use the bbox centre, the fitted circle, or the solved centroid on this ring again without reading this.

TWO FACTS, ONE FROM THE CODE AND ONE FROM A MEASUREMENT:

1. THE DRAWN CENTRE IS A CONSTANT. public/fused.js builds every vertex of the ring as
     points.push([OUTPUT_CENTRE + cos(angle) * radius, OUTPUT_CENTRE + sin(angle) * radius])
   at fixed evenly-spaced angles - so the circle's centre is OUTPUT_CENTRE, a constant, in BOTH builds (the fix moved a smooth() call between two functions; not one line of the drawing changed). A centre that appears to move therefore cannot be the drawn circle moving.

2. THE CONTAINER DOES NOT MOVE EITHER (measured, served page, same feed, 90 frames):
     svg.output-ring   x spread 0.00   y spread 0.00   w 268 spread 0.00   h 268 spread 0.00
     #voice-ring-wrap  x spread 0.00                     w 268 spread 0.00
   No layout change, no resize, no reflow of the ring's own box. Also re-measured here: the state text was CONSTANT ('Agent speaking - your microphone is off') for the whole window, so the reflow idea had no mechanism anyway.

SO EVERY NUMBER IN THIS THREAD ABOUT A MOVING CENTRE IS A SUMMARY STATISTIC OF AN ASYMMETRIC TRAVELLING CONTOUR, with no real component: bbox centre (0.50 px A / 5.50 px B), fitted circle (0.3 / 5.7 px), solved first-harmonic centroid (1.03 / 3.40 px). They differ between builds because the contours differ - which is the fix - and they differ between frames because the crest travels. The first-harmonic-minimised centre IS the curve's centroid, so it travels with the crest by construction; removing the crest bias from a shape summary leaves another shape summary.

MY OWN TWO WRONG INSTRUMENTS IN THIS THREAD, recorded so the next person does not repeat them: (a) I hypothesised page reflow and had it disproved; (b) I then measured path.getBoundingClientRect() thinking it was the container - it is the PATH's own bbox, i.e. another shape summary. The measurement that settles it is the <svg> ELEMENT's box, and that is the one above.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH: the fix's claim (the contour's smoothing cadence) is unaffected - it rests on the geometry profile, the pixel blend, the per-frame RMSE, the rotation-aligned ray profile and the visual read. This closes the attribution question for the centre only.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CLOSING LINE, from the source, verified independently by cap-ds-flash — plus one correction of my own:

THE DISCRIMINATOR WAS NEVER THE CENTRE — IT WAS THE CADENCE. The centre question is closed as 'no real motion component', but nothing about the fix's claim ever depended on it: the cadence is settled by five instruments that did not need the centre at all — the SVG geometry profile, the pixel blend, the per-frame RMSE, the rotation-aligned ray profile, and the visual read (jump frames 03 and 10, matching the numeric spike pairs exactly).

SOURCE CHECKS IT RAN, so the closure is not resting on my summary of my own reasoning:
  - the fix's diff is ONE file (public/audio-client.js, +7/-1) and public/fused.js is not in it — so 'not one line of the drawing changed' is literally true;
  - const OUTPUT_CENTRE = 120 is byte-identical before and after (710a0da^ vs the working tree), with the vertex construction unchanged;
  - the delta is exactly the cadence: smooth(meter.output, meter.smoothOutput, 0.3) moved out of the per-chunk path into the per-frame path.

AND MY OWN NUMBER NEEDS ITS OWN CAVEAT, in the same spirit as the ones that closed this thread. My geometry instrument sampled path points and computed their distances from (50, 50) — a reference I picked in my probe, NOT the ring's centre, which is the fixed 120. So my 'radii' were distances from an arbitrary point, and my residual was a frame-to-frame difference of that summary. That does not weaken the cadence result — frame-to-frame timing of a shape summary is exactly what the question needed, and rotation alignment was applied to the same vector — but the numbers should not be read as radii, the same limit cap-ds-flash stated for its ray profile. Third instrument in this thread with a naming/attribution limit, and the third time stating it made the result survive rather than collapse.

title: a session is running only while somebody is connected to it (runningSession never cleared)
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui 2026-09-23 while checking whether a landed fix needed a restart. Branch fix/live-session-running-flag @ 16fbe15, pushed.

THE DEFECT: server.mjs assigned `runningSession` when a live session started and NOTHING EVER NULLED IT — 'grep -n runningSession server.mjs' returns the initialiser, two readers and the assignment. The close and error handlers called only `session.close()`.

OBSERVED on the served instance: /api/health reported `live: {created:1, running:true}` on three checks over 8 seconds with nobody attached, and stayed true. POST /api/agent-settings told a person 'a session already running keeps the provider it started with' when they had no session — a change deferred to nothing.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MESSAGE: running is the flag that distinguishes STORED from IN USE — the knob a person uses to decide whether it is safe to change the provider. A flag that stays true after the session ends means the interface can never tell them it is safe.

FIX: record which socket owns the session; clear on close/error only when THAT socket goes away. The ownership test is load-bearing: with two peers attached, clearing unconditionally reports the second peer's session as gone when the first leaves. The settings note is now conditional on the state it describes.

FALSIFIER: tests/live-session-flag.test.mjs — drives a real session through the real /live route with the vendor redirected to a local socket (tests/fixtures/live-vendor-redirect.mjs), closes the socket, requires the payload to flip back and the created count NOT to be rewritten; a second test attaches two peers, closes one, requires the other still reported as running, and asserts the note's other half.

MUTATION OUTCOMES, ALL THREE (this is the part worth keeping): guard removed -> RED, 1 fail/1 pass, clean. Clearing removed (the original defect) -> RED, 2 fail, clean. The SAME first mutation, before the teardown was fixed -> HUNG, cancelled at 240 s. A mutation has three outcomes, not two: RED (the check works), GREEN (the check is weak), HUNG (the INSTRUMENT is broken). The hung run was a failing assertion whose teardown awaited a vendor close while a socket was still attached, so a mutation that should have gone red went silent. LESSON FOR THE NEXT PERSON WRITING A MUTATION: a harness that reports only pass and fail cannot report its own failure. Close every socket your test opened; never await a peer that may not leave.

NOT CHANGED: liveSessionsCreated is still a monotonic attempt count on purpose — a refusal that still created a session is the defect that number exists to catch.
close_reason:
LANDED on main as ce78cf6 'fix(live): a session is running only while somebody is connected to it' (gate ALL CLEAR; the served tree was moved onto it and the served API verified afterwards reporting 'main @ c2d180d' with live {created:1, running:false} after a real drive — the flag flipped back on the owner's own instance, which is the fix demonstrated where it was broken).

THE THREE-OUTCOME MUTATION TABLE, as coord asked it be recorded here:
  · guard removed (clear unconditionally)            -> RED, 1 fail / 1 pass, clean, 557 ms
  · clearing removed (the original defect)           -> RED, 2 fail, clean, 8.3 s
  · the same first mutation BEFORE the teardown fix  -> HUNG, cancelled at 240 s, no verdict
The third row is a finding about the INSTRUMENT, not the fix: a failing assertion ran a teardown that awaited a vendor close while a live socket was still attached, so a mutation that should have gone red went silent — and silence is indistinguishable from 'the check is weak' unless somebody notices. A mutation has three outcomes: RED (the check works), GREEN (the check is weak), HUNG (the test is broken). A harness that reports only pass and fail cannot report its own failure. Fix: every socket the test opens is closed before the server stops; no teardown waits on a peer that may not leave.

Also recorded here earlier: this same defect had been filed twice in one session (voicebox-beads-3vp was the earlier copy, named for the symptom) — the lesson being to search the tracker for the SYMPTOM rather than the mechanism.

title: runningSession is never cleared: /api/health reports a live session forever after the first one
description:
FOUND BY voicebox-ui, 2026-09-23, while checking whether a landed fix needed a restart.

THE DEFECT: server.mjs sets `runningSession` at line 1646 when a live session starts and NEVER CLEARS IT. The close and error handlers call only `session.close()`:
    ws.on('close', () => session.close());   // provider session closed
    ws.on('error', () => session.close());   // flag left set
`grep -n 'runningSession' server.mjs` returns exactly two lines: the initialiser (349) and the assignment (1646). Nothing nulls it.

OBSERVED, on the served instance (8787), no client attached: /api/health reported `live:{created:1,running:true}` on three checks over 8 seconds.

TWO SURFACES LIE AS A RESULT:
  1. /api/health: `running: true` for the life of the process after the first session, with nobody connected.
  2. POST /api/agent-settings: answers 'stored — a session already running keeps the provider it started with' to a person who has no session, so a settings change reads as deferred to nothing.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE MESSAGE: 'running' is the flag that distinguishes STORED from IN USE — the knob a person uses to decide whether it is safe to change the provider. A flag that stays true after the session ends means the interface cannot ever tell them it is safe.

FIX: clear it in both handlers (and anywhere a session reaches a terminal state) — one line, plus a test that starts and closes a session and reads /api/health's `running`.

NOTE ON ATTRIBUTION (kept here because it is evidence about the GATE, not about this bug): the single session counted in `created` was created by a diagnostic wire probe carrying `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8787` — entitled by construction, so a real provider session was created and paid for. That is the claim the hello gate's own comment says it cannot verify; the gate behaved as designed.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of voicebox-beads-0i1 (same defect, filed twice by the same lane in one session — this is the earlier copy). The fix landed on main as ce78cf6 'fix(live): a session is running only while somebody is connected to it', with the falsifier tests/live-session-flag.test.mjs and all three mutation outcomes recorded in 0i1. Closing this one so the evidence lives in exactly one place.

title: Plain-language gate misses dynamically rendered refusal identifiers
description: Review of feat/harness-discovery@27741b8 found adapter-not-configured rendered beside its explanation while page acceptance passed. tools/page-acceptance.mjs lines 212-264 scans source HTML/JS literals, not rendered DOM; the source contains ${row.delegation.refused}, while the actual identifier comes from API data. Implement a bounded rendered-text check after exercising representative refusal states, with narrow documented treatment for legitimate command names/code examples and excluding diagnostic title/data attributes. Keep the current source check honest about its scope. LANDED on main in the 8c87e06 merge (content 988b585, verified by reading the landed files rather than the report: tests/rendered-plain-language.test.mjs carries 6 cases on main).

WHAT LANDED: the plain-language gate now reads WHAT A PERSON CAN SEE, not only what we wrote. tools/rendered-plain-language.mjs holds one vocabulary used twice (source literals AND rendered text); the run's refusal vocabulary is harvested from the responses the run itself received, so an identifier that exists in no source literal is still caught; shapes cover ticket ids, an id SPELLED OUT (seven-cd) and attached ids IN CONTEXT (bead 7cd, ticket 0ye, issue #12ab) — not by shape alone, because a bare shape rule fired on 22rem and 4s; the diagnostic allowance is asserted BOTH WAYS in a real browser (visible fails, title/data-* passes, code/pre exempt by element); ZERO readable text is a FAILURE rather than a pass; and the output carries its own scope.

THREE PAGE FIXES: the listing refusal's fallback, the environment row's unreachable LABEL (it printed the refusal id), and two hard-coded ids in the settings surface (one, machine-unreachable (fix the host), was a literal no source check was looking for). All now say the thing in words with the server's term on the title. Two suites were asserting the old contract and were updated rather than deleted.

DRIVEN: green with 2758/2819 characters of visible text read; a fabricated project carrying a bead id declared THROUGH THE API -> FAIL naming seven-cd twice; undeclared -> green again (so the failure was the data, not a stale run).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: The current source check answers what did we write, while the user-facing requirement asks what is on the page; API data and markup diverge at that boundary. A rendered check must inspect visible served DOM text after data and refusal states are applied, not just initial page load, source literals or diagnostic data/title attributes. Cost is not free: it adds state setup and assertions to existing browser drives (the complete inventory drive locally is approximately 1-3 seconds, not an isolated benchmark of the proposed check). Coverage remains limited to driven pages, states and responses; it cannot prove all future provider/error text, unvisited dialogs or inaccessible shadow/frame content are plain English. Define nonzero state coverage and preserve those limitations in reporting.

title: RULE: a process that writes must write outside anything another process measures
description:
## The shape

**A process that writes must write outside anything another process measures.**
Three instances landed today, from three different authors, all the same shape: a writer leaving output where
something else reads state. In every case the symptom was MISLEADING — a dirty tree nobody dirtied by editing,
a file list that was a test's, a check that failed for a reason unrelated to the change under test.

## The three instances

1. **The one-root test suite committed its own audit logs into the repository** — which is how test-run
   artefacts reached a branch and made a change look like it carried files it never touched.
2. **The acceptance harness left its scratch root declared on the shared server**, so a person's page showed a
   test's directory as if it were theirs — the harness's own state leaking into what a human reads.
3. **A Dolt backup was written into the served tree** (`~/worktrees/voicebox-dev/backup/`, 2026-09-20T21:54:40Z)
   because the backup process's **cwd was that tree**. Dolt wrote its backup format there —
   `manifest` (`5:__DOLT__:…`), `backup_state.json` (`last_dolt_commit`, `timestamp`), a `.darc` archive,
   `LOCK`, `oldgen/` — and the acceptance harness's `git status --porcelain` check counts untracked
   directories, so **every landing attempted from that tree read as dirty for a reason no author caused.**

## The rule

- scratch dirs → temp, owned by the process that made them, removed by it;
- backups → outside every repository, and re-runnable without landing inside one;
- test output → its own tree, never the served tree and never the audited root.

## Why it matters more than a dirty directory

Each instance produced a **red check that pointed at the wrong thing**, and the cost was paid by whoever
looked next: a reviewer chasing a file they did not write, a person reading a test's directory as their own,
a lane unable to land. A check whose failure describes the tooling rather than the change is the same class as
everything else in this ledger — *the instrument has to be able to report the thing it is guarding.*

## The evidence, kept because it was diagnosable in one pass

Format named from its own files (`manifest` + `.darc` + `oldgen/`), timestamp read from
`backup_state.json`, the cwd it implies, and the owner ruled out by session cwd plus worktree list — not by
assurance. Relocated to `~/.local/share/voicebox-dolt-backup-20260920T230559` (bytes preserved, reversible,
nothing deleted) at coord's approval; the served tree's `git status --porcelain` is empty again.

title: I2 — /live hello-frame auth: authenticate BEFORE the provider session is created
description: WHAT: the page→environment /live socket takes the pairing bearer in the FIRST frame and validates it before createLiveSession runs — an unauthenticated peer costs a close, never provider spend (today the Gemini session builds on upgrade). The host→vendor outbound leg can carry a real header (astra drove it on Node v24.21.0). DONE: driven — unauthenticated connect is closed before any upstream session exists; an authenticated pairing passes and audio flows. SURFACE: server.mjs /live + lib/live-session.mjs. Closed on 2026-09-21 during Paul's correction that the beads ARE the queue — these were complete and sitting open, which is the mirror of this morning's problem: work that landed and was not recorded as landed.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
**LANDED ON A BRANCH: `fix/live-hello-auth @ bad26b7`** (0 deletions vs main; pre-push gate ALL GATES GREEN).

**THE DEFECT, DRIVEN BEFORE THE FIX** — a peer that opened /live and sent an unauthenticated frame received:
`rate` → `transport-open` → **`ready`, provider "gemini"**: a real provider session created for a connection
nothing had asked about. Refusal-then-cleanup, not a gate. That transcript is the first red this branch made.

**WHAT IT DOES NOW**: the socket does not reach the provider until the connection is entitled to it. The local
page is entitled by construction (own Origin; this host hands no credentials to a page); every other peer
presents the pairing bearer in the FIRST frame `{"type":"hello","bearer":"vbx_…"}`. Missing/malformed/wrong/
silent → a NAMED refusal (`unauthenticated-call`, `bearer-refused`) with the remedy in `why`, closed before any
session exists. A 5s bound, because silence is not a credential.

**THE SECOND HALF, WITNESSED**: `liveSessionsCreated` counts where the spend happens (before
`createLiveSession`, so a throwing create still counts) and `/api/health` reports `live: { created, running }`.
The tests assert the count, not just the refusal — *refused is satisfied by the broken version too*.

**MUTATION CHECK**: old order restored (session first, gate after) → the first test reds on *"a refused peer
must NEVER receive the rate frame"* and the paired case reds on the created count; mutant removed.

**CONSEQUENCE, DECLARED**: `tests/live-rate-frame.test.mjs` and `tests/live-voice.test.mjs` are local Node
clients of a server they spawn and now declare the local origin — the same thing a browser does for them.

**NOT CLAIMED**: "same origin" is a claim any non-browser client can make (it can set headers), so this gate
stops an unentitled peer costing a session and makes the paired path enforceable — a per-process page token
minted into the served HTML is what closes the claim itself, and belongs with the environment-identity work.
Also not driven here: audio flowing on the authenticated path (needs a real key; the session is created, the
vendor leg is not exercised).

**TWO BUGS OF MY OWN, both caught by the tests**: the project's zero-dep socket has `on` and not `once` (my
first gate threw inside the handler, so every remote peer fell through to the timeout — three identical
failures made it legible), and the local-page check compared against `PORT` (= 0 on an ephemeral bind) instead
of the BOUND port.

Gate: 204 tests, 203 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped (wabt parity half, labelled).

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text: INDEPENDENT REVIEW (gemini): PASS. Reviewed fix/live-hello-auth @ bad26b7. 1) liveSessionsCreated is placed immediately before createLiveSession inside the try block; throwing creates count; unauthenticated/invalid peers never reach beginSession() and leave count at 0. 2) Local page entitlement claimsToBeTheLocalPage is explicitly scoped as a browser Origin claim with documented limits, not a cryptographic boundary. 3) Order verified live: unauthenticated/wrong-bearer sockets receive 0 rate frames and 0 session spend. 4) Mutation testing (restoring beginSession unconditionally on upgrade) fails 3/4 tests RED on rate frame arrival and session count. 5) live-rate-frame and live-voice Origin headers match browser behavior. comments.author: Paul Kinlan

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
CLAIMED, NOT BUILT — and left legible rather than a branch with untested code in it. My session budget ended before a drivable half, which the lane standard (set by the lane that handed this over) prefers to a half-built gate. What follows is the one thing the bead was missing: **exactly which measured report makes the refusal fire, per axis, read out of the receipts rather than the design.**

THE RECEIPT IS THE SPEC (measured, `reports/sandbox-survey-20260920/probe-bwrap.json`):
- **deny-files** reads `filesystem` — fields `home`, `pathEntries`, `dirs`, `canReadPasswd`, `mountsReadable`.
- **deny-processes** reads `tools` — one result per binary (`sh`, `bash`, `node`, `python3`, …, `bwrap`, `sudo`, `mount`), each carrying `value` when the binary RAN.
- **passthrough-network** reads `network` — `loopback`, `dns`, `outboundTcp443IpLiteral`, `outboundTcp80ByName`, `cloudMetadataService`, `interfaces`, `resolvConf`, each carrying `reachable`.

THE FIRING CONDITION, per axis — `decide(report, act)` refuses `absent-capability` when the measured outcome is the OPPOSITE of the deny the tier claims, and names the axis and the remedy:
1. `deny-processes`: a `tools.<binary>.value` present for a binary the act needs (i.e. the shell ran *inside* the fence) → refuse, axis `deny-processes`, remedy "bwrap bounds which binary, not what it can do; the fence must deny the interpreter, not the wrapper".
2. `passthrough-network`: `network.outboundTcp443IpLiteral.reachable === true` or `outboundTcp80ByName.reachable === true` — and unambiguously `cloudMetadataService.reachable === true` → refuse, axis `passthrough-network`, remedy "an egress policy, not a hint: the probe reached the metadata service".
3. `deny-files`: `filesystem.mountsReadable` (or `home`/`pathEntries`) showing a path outside the root was readable → refuse, axis `deny-files`, remedy "scope the root; a readable home is not a deny".

WHY THIS KEEPS THE PROMISE FRIABLE (the handover's key property, preserved):
`decide(report, act)` takes S1's `BoundaryReport` as data, so when the fence boots the drive is an **addition rather than a rewrite** — three fixtures, one per axis, each a *real* receipt from this file with the measured field flipped, plus the falsification that matters: **a report whose axis IS denied must produce no refusal at all** (otherwise the gate fires on everything and is decoration). I could not write those three fixtures without a fence to produce a report from, which is the reason this is a comment and not a branch.

WHAT REMAINS (a small, bounded slice for whoever picks it up):
1. `core/tier-table.ts`: `decide(report, act)` → `{ ok: false, refused: "absent-capability", axis, why, remedy }`, with `axis` a value from the receipt's own vocabulary (the three above), and the refusal quoting the measured field and its value.
2. Three fixtures built from `probe-bwrap.json` — one per axis — asserting the refusal names the axis AND the remedy.
3. The negative fixture (axis denied ⇒ no refusal), which is the one that proves it is a gate rather than a slogan.
4. Wire it into whatever reads the tier table, ONLY once S1 emits the report — the bead stays OPEN until then, which is the rule this handover came with.

comments.text:

**THE BEAD STAYS OPEN**: nothing calls `decide()` yet because S1 has not landed a fence that emits a
BoundaryReport — the fence drive is the second half, exactly as the handover said.

**THE RECEIPT IS THE SPEC, AND READING IT CORRECTED THE BRIEF** — two field names in the handover were
written from the design rather than the data (probe-bwrap.json, 2026-09-20T14:52:32Z):
  * the outbound checks carry **`ok`**, not `reachable` (only `loopback` uses `reachable`). A check written
    from that brief would have read a field that does not exist and **passed by finding nothing** — the same
    class as every instrument failure in this fleet;
  * a binary that RAN carries `value`; a missing one carries `error: "<bin>: not present"`.
  * also from the data rather than the brief: `filesystem.dirs[path]` is `{listable, writable:{value}}`.

**TWO WAYS A BOUNDARY FAILS AN ACT, as different sentences:**
  * **CONTRADICTED** — the deny the environment claims is measurably not in force. The bwrap receipt IS this
    case for deny-processes: the probe ran *inside* the fence and its own report shows `tools.sh.value` and
    `tools.node.value` present — the earlier finding ("bwrap bounds which binary, not what it can do") as
    data. Refused, quoting the measured field and value.
  * **ABSENT** — no mechanism at all: *"no process mechanism in this environment … run it where the report
    shows exec"*, this bead's own DONE criterion.
  * **UNMEASURED is not a pass** — a report that cannot answer refuses in its own words, because "we did not
    look" and "we looked and it was denied" are different facts.

**THE NEGATIVE CONTROL CORRECTED MY OWN CONFLATION** (and the corrected property is stronger): "axis denied ⇒
no refusal at all" cannot hold for `exec`, because a process-less environment genuinely cannot run a spawn —
refusing it is correct. What the test now asserts is: **on an axis that IS denied, the refusal may only ever
be the ABSENCE sentence, never the CONTRADICTION one.** A report where the fence HELD must never be read as a
fence that leaked. Read/network on a denied axis: no refusal at all (`ok: true`, with a why).

**FIXTURES from the receipt, one field flipped each**: `outboundTcp443IpLiteral {ok:false, error:"timed out"}`
→ `{ok:true}`; `cloudMetadataService` answering (its own sentence — credentials may be reachable); the
receipt's own `mountsReadable.value === true` + `canReadPasswd` for deny-files.

**MUTATION-CHECKED BOTH WAYS**: refuse-everything → 8/8 red; pass-everything → 8/8 red. The tests bind to
the behaviour, not to the code.

**THE SEAM WITH THE TABLE'S OWN RULE**: main already carried `{ id: "absent-capability", tier: 0, why: "this
placement has no mechanism for it", matches: (a) => !ENFORCEABLE.has(a.kind) }`. The rule decides WHETHER;
`decide()` decides WHICH axis and WHY, and returns the same id so a reader meets one word in both places. A
test asserts exactly that agreement and that `decide()` does not merely echo the generic sentence.

**DISCLOSED, twice**: (1) my first landing of this code went into the CANONICAL checkout by accident (a
chained command started in ~/voicebox), caught because the worktree test could not find the export, copied to
the worktree and reverted in the canonical checkout (verified clean); (2) a rebuild attempt left the branch at
main with none of my commits — recovered from the pushed branch, which is why pushing before rebuilding
mattered.

`writable`, and the why-string always printed `dirs[home].listable = true`. Driven: mounts + the listing half

stated and written into the module's contract):
  * claimed bounded network + ALIVE egress → CONTRADICTED, refused (unchanged);
  * claimed bounded network + DEAD egress → **refused as UNVERIFIED**, because "did not reach" conflates

as a verified path. Recorded here so the next reader does not spend an afternoon trying to reach it.

RATIONALE:
1. Product Contradiction: Voicebox server requires outbound WebSockets to Gemini Live / OpenAI Realtime. Under --unshare-net, outbound connections fail with ENETUNREACH. An inbound bridge allows the browser page to reach the server, but the server cannot reach any model — creating a server that serves but cannot think or speak.
2. The Proxy Trap: To restore model egress in an unshared netns, a full outbound filtering forward proxy (like Anthropic's srt proxy) would be required. As documented in journal/topics/sandbox-mechanisms.md, srt's proxy introduced loopback IPv6 bugs, NO_PROXY breakages, and path-widening CVEs.
3. Truth in Measurement: The interactive server ladder is complete at L1.5 (filesystem fenced + process fenced + systemd-run seccomp/caps lockdown). The network axis is honestly reported as 'passes' (shared with host), rather than claiming L2 via a proxy-holed network.
4. Offline Role for --unshare-net: Network namespace isolation is preserved in tools/fence.sh and reserved strictly for offline/batch execution (delegate_task under D1/D2) where no live server or model connection is required.
5. Re-open Conditions: 1) Local on-device LLM runner eliminating internet requirement; or 2) Hardened, fleet-approved outbound proxy substrate.

One behaviour, two edges. The refusal names its cause and remedy.

INTERFACE QUESTION FOR THE lgx LANE (raised directly with voicebox-dsflash1-a2e7): who owns the pending record and who decides expiry. Read of the bead's binding requirement — the AUTHORITATIVE EXECUTING ENVIRONMENT owns it (a page can be the host); the PERMISSION UI IS NEVER THE AUTHORITY; BROWSER DISAPPEARANCE MUST DENY UNRESOLVED APPROVALS RATHER THAN DROPPING THEM. If agreed, the transport only carries request/answer and never decides.

comments.author: Paul Kinlan
comments.text:
# Browser-owned delegation: constraints on D2

A **harness** does the agent/model/tool work; an **environment** is where that harness runs and obtains its capabilities. **Many harnesses can run in one environment.** Putting Voicebox on a server to reach Paul's machine chooses one deployment. It must not make a server part of the shared harness contract. This note constrains the existing D2 ACP work, `voicebox-beads-6co`; it does not propose a second delegation implementation.

> “there is a world where there is zero server and it's all run locally on the client, and that has to be a hard requirement.”
>
> — Paul, relayed by coord, 2026-09-21, seq571

**Record:** `voicebox-beads-8fv.1`. **Status:** design and source inspection only; no browser delegation implementation or new runtime experiment. The quote is also in the bead. The current D2 clarification explicitly permits direct remote model APIs: *zero Voicebox server or local bridge* is the hard requirement, not necessarily offline inference. No further choice between a universal client or server architecture is pending. D9 conversation injection and D10 post-harness lifetime remain separate decisions.

Sources inspected: author D1 `c44c1de4118a93c382294cacf70b5d529b425004`, landed main `58a37358e514a0b5a140dcad8749861732371cef`, and D2/configuration bead descriptions captured on 2026-09-21. Earlier [delegation](delegate-task-plan.md) and [environment](environments-plan.md) plans remain history; Paul's dictated appendix was not changed.

## 1. What this changes in D2

D2 is **“Environment-owned async ACP client, ONE admitted adapter (stdio)”**. Its 08:52 UTC clarification already says that stdio is the first machine adapter, not the shared-library transport contract. That direction is correct. The remaining change is to make the separation executable rather than infer it from a Node-only success.

| D2 clause | Keep or change |
|---|---|
| Environment owns asynchronous work; admission returns a durable handle | Keep. An HTTP request, page view or ACP connection must not become the task's identity. The executing environment owns the record and runs the admitted harness instance. |
| ONE admitted real adapter, initially stdio | Keep as the first **machine binding**. Do not make spawning a process a prerequisite for constructing/importing the harness or admitting a browser-capable configuration. A browser selecting that stdio-only adapter refuses before dispatch. |
| ACP client learned from CAP, not imported wholesale | Keep. Separate ACP state/framing/validation from process, filesystem, socket and credential I/O. A local in-page tool call does not need an invented ACP subprocess. |
| Cancel during a turn settles cancelled | Keep the outcome requirement, but require observed turn settlement. Sending `session/cancel`, rejecting a promise or aborting a signal is not itself proof that effects stopped. Unknown effects remain interrupted/unknown; D6 owns the broader cancellation surface. |
| Surface: `lib/` + `server.mjs` | Expand to the shared loop/task contracts plus environment bindings. `server.mjs` becomes one caller of the shared lifecycle, not its only owner. Browser storage/auth/lifetime cannot be implemented by importing Node I/O. |
| Placement decision blocks transport design | Superseded. `voicebox-beads-3uq` now owns implementing the portable protocol decision, not asking Paul to choose one placement. |
| A real adapter completes one bounded task | Necessary machine acceptance, insufficient zero-server acceptance. Also require browser import and same-page lifecycle conformance with every Voicebox API/bridge unavailable. Label fixtures; they do not establish a real browser agent. |

D2 consumes `voicebox-beads-8fv.2`'s configured-agent record; it must not create another registry. Stable configured-agent IDs, harness implementation/version, model reference, executing environment and observed readiness belong there. D3 exposes that inventory. A configured agent is not its transient ACP session, and neither is an environment key.

**N18 is a source gap, despite `mzs` being closed.** At inspected main, `server.mjs`'s `/api/turn` still owns `resolveTurn → execute`; `public/fused.js` posts turns to that endpoint. `lib/resolver.mjs` exports resolution, not the whole lifecycle. The N18-labelled test checks that `core/` imports nothing outside itself. That proves a useful import boundary, not delivery of the importable loop described by `mzs`. D2/3uq need the actual entry point and a browser drive of it, not a closure citation.

## 2. Ownership and the shape of a call

Keep these identities separate:

- **Environment key:** the existing stable self-issued identity contract. The browser binding persists its own key; it must not use the shared string `local`, a tab title or an origin URL as identity.
- **Configured agent:** the stable configuration from 8fv.2. Renaming it must not retarget a task.
- **Harness instance and execution generation:** the live loop/session and its current incarnation. Several instances can share an environment. Killing one must not mark its neighbours dead.
- **Authenticated principal and authority epoch:** who may issue/read this task under current grants. Neither an environment address nor a harness ID proves that authority.
- **Task, root and attempt:** the immutable accepted work, the captured root binding, and the executing attempt. A new page connection changes none of them.

For the minimum tab-owned profile, several harness instances can run under one browser environment runtime. Its task service owns admission, aggregate capacity and storage serialization; each harness does not create an independent eight-slot allowance or an independent task database. A profile/origin may retain several named logical environments, but their identity/storage mapping needs an explicit rule. Do not accidentally assign every new tab the same singleton key, or mint a new environment for every observer connection.

### Envelope

Retain the existing call concepts: version, call ID, executing environment, admitted descriptor/configuration reference, tool, arguments and bounds echo. The receiver resolves those references against **its** current admission; the echo is not a grant. `delegate_task` model arguments remain bounded agent/task/context data. Owner, root authority, command, cwd, token, endpoint and execution generation are not model arguments.

The authenticated caller context accompanies delivery through the trusted transport/host binding, separately from model-controlled data. For a remote call it comes from verified pairing; for a local call it comes from an explicitly entitled caller/port created by the browser host. The receiving environment still checks authority on every status read. Do not permit the caller to manufacture that context by adding `owner` to an object.

There is a source ambiguity to settle in 3uq before extending the wire: `core/wire.ts` describes `CallEnvelope.environment` as **the environment asked to act**, while `lib/channel.mjs` describes stamping the channel's **own** environment. These agree for a co-located call but do not define a cross-environment caller/target split. Specify the executing target unambiguously and verify it against the receiving binding; retain authenticated source identity separately. If the published shape needs two identity fields, version it. The strict v1 parser must not silently start accepting extra authority fields.

An accepted response reports observations: address, executing environment, pinned root, queued state and confirmed record position. It is not permission for future effects. Status, progress and final results correlate to the same task/harness/attempt; a notification channel is replaceable. Opening another view must never resubmit the task.

### When both sides are in the same page

```text
harness A
  → trusted caller binding
  → the same admission/authority/bounds checks
  → environment task service → confirmed queued record → return handle
  → admitted harness B, scheduled independently
  → mediated tool effects and recorded observations
```

The transport can be an ordinary asynchronous function or a transferred `MessagePort`. No localhost socket, health endpoint, JSON-over-HTTP ceremony or server token is needed just because the contract is called a protocol. `createExecutorDoor` already accepts object input and normalises it; preserve its validation rather than introduce a permissive local shortcut. A direct invocation still needs an entitled caller context. WebMCP could expose the same admitted functions later; it is not required for the architecture and does not supply the permission boundary.

Keep expensive inference/Wasm execution off the interaction thread. A worker solves scheduling/isolation of execution from the UI; it does **not** by itself sandbox arbitrary same-origin agent JavaScript. Trusted loop code interpreting model output as data can use mediated tools. Admitting arbitrary generated JavaScript requires a separately demonstrated boundary. Wasm's restricted imports are useful only when the actual imports, wrapper and network paths are bounded.

## 3. Persistence without a machine filesystem

D1's ordering survives the move:

```text
validate caller, root, configuration and enforceable bounds
→ atomically exclude conflicting admission/retry
→ append and confirm the captured task record
→ settle the admission response
→ schedule execution
→ append observed transitions; never replay on read/reopen
```

The async storage operation changes the implementation: no result may escape while a transaction/write is still pending. Input, policy and configuration must be captured before awaiting persistence; later UI/configuration changes must not widen them. Dispatch and effects still recheck current authority within that captured ceiling; a snapshot does not defeat later revocation. Read-only views use the original root, never whichever project is currently selected. D4 context manifests remain separate; D1 currently refuses nonempty context rather than pretending references were captured.

**Keep one authoritative event history.** The smallest candidate is to adapt the existing OPFS/root audit for task events, with serialized writes, strict parsing and a defined confirmation operation. IndexedDB already holds picked-folder handles and can hold identity/credential references. Do not also persist a competing task-state table and then reconcile two sources of truth. If measurement favours IndexedDB transactions for the browser audit, move the authoritative browser event history there deliberately; projections/exports are not another authority.

Existing browser methods are not sufficient unchanged:

- `browser/storage.ts::readLines` catches every read error and returns `[]`.
- `browser/worker.ts::readAudit` drops entries that fail parsing.
- `appendLine` reads a length, writes using `createWritable({keepExistingData:true})`, then closes. It has no multi-context admission transaction or D1-style file/directory flush contract.

For tasks, missing history, unreadable history, torn history and permission loss must be different outcomes. As coord put it, **“an error read as an absence is a fail-open wearing a fail-closed name.”** A corrupt log cannot be treated as a fresh sequence or permission to start again.

Storage claims must name the platform guarantee. IndexedDB exposes strict/relaxed durability modes; strict requests confirmation to persistent storage, while relaxed can complete after handing changes to the OS. This is not a portable promise of immunity to power loss. OPFS needs its own measured close/flush contract, including contention and failure. `navigator.storage.persist()` concerns eviction, not process survival; denial, quota exhaustion, user-cleared storage and private-browsing loss remain possible. [S1–S2]

Root identity also needs a browser binding: keep `RootDescriptor`'s OPFS/handle kinds, preserve the owning environment, and retain the actual captured handle/root incarnation where needed. Recreating a directory under the same label/path must not silently adopt an older task. The machine's device/inode check has no fictitious browser equivalent; handle identity and delete/recreate behaviour need a targeted drive.

## 4. Credentials and access

The current server deployment keeps its pairing bearer in the host and proxies browser calls. That remains valid there. A zero-server deployment cannot require that proxy, a `.host-token` file, or a backend that mints every local call.

For local work, the trusted browser environment supplies a local owner/grant context and keeps its identity/sealing material outside model-visible tools and task records. Web Crypto plus IndexedDB is a candidate for persistent key custody. A non-extractable `CryptoKey` prevents raw export through the API; it does not prevent hostile same-origin code from using the key or forwarding a key object. The Web Crypto specification explicitly warns about script injection and cross-origin sharing through `postMessage`. An IDB database name or a separate same-origin worker is not a secret boundary. [S5]

Consequently, keep credentials and root handles out of agent contexts, inventory, audits, model prompts and public message payloads. Keep untrusted executable code away from the trusted origin's ambient storage/network authority. Browser grants must be checked when used, including after a reload. A picker handle persisted yesterday is not today's read/write permission. I3 still determines revocation semantics; neither the task seal nor cached configuration overrides current revocation.

For a remote model, choose a provider-supported browser credential flow and a bounded direct connection, or name the missing capability. An OAuth public-client flow or appropriately scoped browser credential may fit; a provider requiring a secret backend exchange does not fit the zero-server profile unchanged. Do not silently introduce a bridge as a fallback. On-device inference avoids a vendor credential but still depends on observed API/model/hardware availability. This note chooses neither a provider nor a credential-rotation protocol.

The task address remains a locator, not a bearer grant. A browser address should resolve through the owning environment's protected store/binding rather than require a machine path inside it. Preserve compatibility for existing D1 handles; changing their interpretation is a versioned migration, not a renderer change. Clearing the owner key/store cannot result in anonymous adoption. Another browser profile has neither the private origin storage nor the original authority: it must refuse unless an explicit transfer/pairing mechanism exists. D1's two-profile server-proxy test is not a serverless cross-profile guarantee.

## 5. What interrupted means when a tab closes

For an executing environment owned by a document/dedicated-worker lifetime, closing that document can end execution while the saved task remains. No close handler is required to run. On the next authorized opening, reconcile the prior nonterminal task to **interrupted, outcome unknown** only when the execution owner can no longer continue under its old generation. Never turn absence of a heartbeat into proof of death and never replay the prompt to discover what happened.

Several cases must remain distinguishable:

| Event | Required interpretation |
|---|---|
| Observer/message port closes; executing environment remains alive | Record stays addressable to another entitled connection; does not inherently cancel execution. D10 may later impose an explicit disconnect policy. |
| One harness stops while other harnesses share the environment | Reconcile only that harness's attempts. Environment-wide failure would be false. |
| Page is hidden, frozen, background-throttled or in bfcache | Not evidence of death. State may be old; report unconfirmed liveness rather than fabricate a terminal outcome. Recheck deadlines and authority before effects on resume. |
| Owning document/worker is destroyed and a later instance opens the store | Confirm/fence the old execution generation, then record interrupted without dispatch. If that confirmation is unavailable, return an honest owner-unconfirmed refusal. |
| The original runtime actually survives elsewhere | Query it under the recorded authority. Do not both resume it and start a replacement. |
| Origin storage/key is lost | Record/owner unavailable, not an empty successful task or an invitation to replay. |

A possible coordination mechanism is Web Locks for short storage critical sections and a separately held execution-ownership lock, plus a persisted generation checked at every mediated effect/transition. **Do not use a lock's availability alone as proof of process death.** Code may release locks before freezing; Chrome recommends doing so. `steal` explicitly permits prior code to continue without exclusivity, so it is not a safe death detector. A takeover must make stale generations unable to issue further mediated effects, and may still have unknown in-flight effects. Worker termination details and freeze/reacquisition races require browser experiments. [S3–S4]

Do not hold one exclusive lock for all harness computation: many harnesses may run in one environment. Serialize the records that actually conflict and bind execution ownership to the relevant runtime/harness/attempt. Aggregate environment budgets still apply.

A SharedWorker may change which page owns the work, but is not a promise of indefinite survival after the last client disappears. A service worker is event-driven and may be terminated while idle; calling it a durable worker does not make an arbitrary agent turn durable. No browser-only binding may promise compute continues after the browser is closed. [S6] D10 can choose among lifetimes the environment can actually provide; it cannot select an impossible one by metadata.

## 6. Specific moves, with existing homes

These are design findings attached to D2/3uq, not a separate markdown task tracker.

| Current file or concept | Required move | Existing work it constrains |
|---|---|---|
| `core/tasks.ts::TaskRecord.pid`, `boot`; `reduceTask` requires `root.kind === "machine"` and a `machine:` root string | Keep shared state/input/terminal rules; represent harness/attempt/generation independently of OS process metadata. Validate the captured root's portable identity, retaining per-writer sequence rules. | D2, D7, 3uq |
| `lib/tasks.mjs::createTaskHost`, Node fs/path/crypto, `process.kill`, `setImmediate` | Separate shared admission/run/reduction from confirmed event storage, authenticated caller context, executor and lifetime bindings. Node keeps realpath/device/inode/fsync/PID observation; the browser implements real platform equivalents or refuses. No fake PID, Node polyfill or second task engine. | D2, 3uq |
| `server.mjs::SELF_ENVIRONMENT`, `.host-token`, paired `/api/execute` | Keep the existing self-identity contract. Supply browser-owned identity/auth/sealing through its binding; do not expose the machine host token or confuse environment identity with owner proof. | I3, 3uq, 8fv.2 |
| `server.mjs` `/api/turn`, `execute`, live tool callback; `public/fused.js::turn` | Move the shared cycle into the actual importable harness library. HTTP/live/page entry points call it. Runtime I/O, UI rendering and provider selection stay outside that cycle. | D2 + N18 delivery verification |
| `lib/channel.mjs`, `core/wire.ts` | Define caller versus executing-target identity; preserve strict parsing and bounds validation for direct object, port and remote transport. Remove transport assumptions from shared ownership, not the authority checks. | 3uq, D2 |
| `browser/storage.ts::readLines`, `appendLine`; `browser/worker.ts::readAudit`, `appendAudit` | Add a confirmed, fail-closed task/audit path with explicit missing/corrupt/permission errors and writer coordination. Protect private task/credential namespaces against generic tool read/write. Do not use the current swallow/filter path as admission evidence. | D2 storage binding, D7 |
| `browser/idb.ts`, OPFS/picked-root registry and mutable `current` in `browser/worker.ts` | Persist environment/credential/root bindings without task-state duplication; task reads use captured roots. Define and drive same-path replacement, lost handles, grants and corruption. | 3uq, I3, D7 |
| Global executor registration and per-`createTaskHost` active map | Environment-owned shared admission/capacity, distinct harness instances and per-attempt lifecycle. Multiple harnesses must not multiply limits or reclaim each other's tasks. | D2, 8fv.2 |
| `core/environment.ts` browser/server kind, origin/reach and server-oriented refusal text | Reuse the descriptor. Browser kind already exists and need not have an origin endpoint. Represent in-process reach/lifetime and measured capabilities without treating every absence as a stopped HTTP service. | 3uq, configuration/discovery |
| `lib/commands.mjs`, live/text declarations and native task dispatch | Keep one admitted command path with correct caller context. Do not advertise a callable browser delegation tool before the browser binding can authenticate, persist and enforce it. | D2, D3, existing catalogue work |
| Browser delivery/type stripping and static resources | Produce a browser-importable artifact from the same source; no runtime Vite, Node TS transformer, `/api/turn` or hidden bridge dependency. Static asset delivery is not a running Voicebox task server. | N18 verification, 3uq |
| Existing D1 tests and `docs/10-delegate-task-d1.md` | Retain machine evidence; add portable conformance and browser lifecycle tests. Document machine-only guarantees rather than generalise fsync/PID or paired-proxy success to a tab. | D2 acceptance |

No generic transport framework or plugin container is required by this list. Start with explicit injected functions where the existing code touches platform facts. Keep `core/` free of platform imports and also test the shared runtime entry point; a clean `core/` cannot compensate for a server-only orchestrator.

## 7. Acceptance additions to record on D2

1. Import the same loop/task-lifecycle implementation in Node and a real browser with no Node globals or running Voicebox API/bridge. Static assets may be preloaded; every runtime backend attempt is observed and fails the test. A deterministic closed adapter establishes the lifecycle contract, **not** production model/ACP acceptance.
2. Run two configured harness instances in one environment. They have distinct instance IDs, share aggregate limits and current admission, and neither consumes the other's responses or terminal state. Drive one browser instance through the same contract.
3. Browser admission returns only after confirmed persistence, before held work finishes. Open an independently entitled port/view in the same storage partition; read the same task, close the first observer and read again. Another principal or profile with only the handle refuses.
4. Abort/quota-fail persistence, corrupt a record and simulate permission loss. Each refuses before dispatch; no empty-history reset. Concurrent duplicate call IDs produce one admission/dispatch, and changed content conflicts.
5. Actually destroy the owning tab/worker, reopen retained storage and observe interruption without replay. Separately freeze/resume and exercise bfcache: neither may be mislabelled death. Include a stale-generation late-effect attempt and another still-running harness as controls.
6. Block machine processes/stdio in the browser profile and select the machine-only configured agent: named refusal, zero hidden bridge requests. The separate machine run still drives the exact configured ACP adapter/version, bounded completion and observed cancellation.
7. Inspect disclosure: no provider/root credential in model context, event history, inventory or task address. Test an entitled local call positively; reject fabricated owner/config/bounds data. Exercise direct browser-provider custody only with a supported flow, without treating a fixture as vendor acceptance.

The first machine adapter may satisfy its scoped D2 implementation slice. It cannot close the zero-server requirement until a real browser-capable harness/configuration has been exercised. Record that remaining acceptance on the existing protocol/configuration work, not a second ACP project.

## 8. Questions that remain

**Policy/configuration decisions:** the stable browser environment's scope across tabs and storage partitions; which credential flow establishes its local/remote principal; which provider/agent is actually browser-capable; required browser/device support; how authority rotation affects old task handles; D9's delivery surface and D10's lifetime policy. The current clarification already answers that remote model APIs are allowed; this is not a question to send back to Paul again. A fully offline voice/model configuration is a stronger, separately measured capability.

**Cannot be settled by this document:** confirmation strength and latency of the chosen browser event store; interrupted-write and quota behaviour; picked-root replacement identity; multi-tab admission races; freeze/bfcache/worker ownership and fencing; prompt/request cancellation versus residual effects; actual browser provider auth/CORS/protocol support. These require the bounded positive/negative drives above. No real client-only agent, transport or containment result is claimed here.

## Platform references

Retrieved 2026-09-21. These constrain the proposal; they are not this lane's runtime evidence.

- **S1:** [IndexedDB transaction durability](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/IDBTransaction/durability) and [IndexedDB specification](https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#dom-idbtransaction-durability).
- **S2:** [Storage persistence](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/StorageManager/persist) and [Storage Standard](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-pressure).
- **S3:** [Web Locks: termination and steal semantics](https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/). Lock ownership coordinates cooperative contexts; it is not authentication or proof all prior effects ended.
- **S4:** [Chrome Page Lifecycle](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/web-platform/page-lifecycle-api): frozen tasks, unobservable discards, unreliable close callbacks, and releasing locks before freezing.
- **S5:** [Web Crypto security considerations](https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/#security-developers): persistent CryptoKeys, injection risk and structured-clone sharing across origins.
- **S6:** [Service Worker lifetime](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#service-worker-lifetime) and [HTML worker lifetimes](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/workers.html#the-worker's-lifetime).

Modern-web guidance was consulted. Its installed skill is outdated; retrieved on-device/WebMCP guidance was treated as capability-specific, not grounds to promise support on every browser or to add a mandatory fallback server. No skill update, product fix or browser prototype was performed.

CANCELLATION HALF BUILT AND PUSHED (ds-flash-1b, 2026-09-24): **branch fix/6co-cancellation @ fd85eb94a6672e9c71c6ec569cc009e5bca0f35c**, gate GREEN on its own stages (docs-touched → [lanes] ok: 31 unit, 52 live → unit → live → acceptance). Awaiting independent review; I am not the reviewer.

WHAT IT DOES — three states, three names, because 'there is nothing to cancel' has two different remedies:
- cancel() during a running turn sends session/cancel and returns what it DID ({ ok: true, sent: true }) rather than claiming termination;
- the TURN settles as **task-cancelled** when the harness answers stopReason 'cancelled' — a different fact from acp-turn-incomplete (the harness answered something the client does not accept). Collapsing them would make a cancel read as a fault, and the text collected before the stop is not an answer (the why says so);
- cancelling when nothing has run refuses **task-not-found**; cancelling after a turn finished refuses **task-not-running**.

ONE DELIBERATE DEVIATION, with its evidence: the assignment named 'task-already-complete' for the finished case, but the repo already owns **task-not-running** for exactly that idea (lib/tasks.mjs:148, asserted in tests/task-card.test.mjs). One idea, one name — so the client uses the existing one rather than adding a second spelling. Say the word if you want the literal code instead and it is a one-line change.

TESTS (hermetic, no credentials, in the existing ACP suite): an in-flight cancel settles the turn as task-cancelled and the notification carries sessionId with NO id; a completed task refuses without sending anything; and a third case proves the new name did not swallow the old one (a max_tokens stop is still acp-turn-incomplete). The pre-existing 'nothing has run' assertion moves from task-not-running to task-not-found, which is the point. Suite: 6/6 in tests/acp-client.test.mjs; the task layer still agrees at 22/22 (tests/tasks.test.mjs + tests/task-card.test.mjs). docs/11-acp-adapter.md carries the three names (it was rewritten on main while this was prepared — the insertion is anchored on its own cancellation sentence, and the stash conflict that produced was resolved by restoring main's version and re-inserting).

description:
EPIC: delegate_task — an environment-owned async task system (journal-dvq implementation).
The voice agent issues ONE delegate_task command; the selected environment admits it, records a durable task, and owns an async ACP client; the command returns the task address BEFORE the agent finishes; the voice agent keeps listening. Settled for the current machine-access deployment: server-side registry and PROXIED custody (bearer held host-side). These are not requirements on browser-only deployment. Probe automatic; stable host identity; single user; deltas are the exchange unit and the file-owning environment admits applying them. The binding portable requirement below supersedes any universal server-only reading.
Source: reports/voicebox-build/delegate-task-plan.md (journal-dvq); coupling markers ENV-IDENTITY/AGENTS/AUTH/LIFETIME/READBACK; SANDBOX-MECHANISM owned by the fence provider epic.
Done-for-the-epic: the acceptance drives in delegate-task-plan §9 — delegate returns a persisted handle, a second unrelated voice turn works mid-task, cancellation is honest, reconciliation after restart names interrupted rather than replaying.


2026-09-21 placement clarification (supersedes universal server assumptions above):
BINDING REQUIREMENT (Paul, 2026-09-21): the harness must run anywhere, including entirely in a browser client with zero Voicebox server or local bridge. Server deployment is allowed for machine access, not required by the shared contract. Placement changes available capabilities, transport, storage and lifetime; it must not fork the coordination semantics. A browser cannot spawn a stdio CLI; refuse that unavailable capability rather than hiding a server dependency. Zero server does not mean zero remote model API.
The previously settled server-side registry/proxied custody is the present machine-access deployment only. It does not exclude a browser-only harness/registry/auth path. New configuration, fleet and coordinator slices attach here because they feed the same durable delegation contract, not a second task engine: voicebox-beads-8fv.2, voicebox-beads-8fv.3, voicebox-beads-8fv.4.

title: Build the shared log: presence, activity, and seen-marks across two agents
description: N19 settled the model (shared state, merged artefacts) and k3's §9 turned its five recommendations into SPECIFICATION: the actor model, a liveness column, the shared log as the medium, SEEN-MARKS, and per-agent turn authority. What exists: the per-root audit with (instance, seq), no claimed global order, one file per root - acceptance check 9 already exercises the merge side. What is missing is the SHARED side: an append-only log carrying presence, what each agent is doing, and what each has READ. Seen-marks is the seam rather than a field: 'what did it know?' is a question two agents must answer about each other, and a late merge can only answer it after the fact. Start there, because it changes the audit's entry shape before anything writes entries. And note ds-flash-2's framing of the merge's new role: it stops being the coordination channel and becomes the LANDING step - a user-visible event rather than a background reconciliation.
